item.title: 0. index
item.description: Escalation & Handoff — Routing Work You Don’t Own Not every request that lands on you is yours to decide on or act on.

item.title: 1. What escalation is
item.description: ← Escalation & Handoff What escalation is Escalation is passing a request — or a decision — to the person who owns it, because it sits above your authority, outside your assigned priorities, or needs a call that isn’t yours to make.

item.title: 2. When to escalate
item.description: ← Escalation & Handoff When to escalate Escalate when a request needs a decision you don’t own, or asks for work that isn’t yours to start.

item.title: 3. The clean handoff
item.description: ← Escalation & Handoff The clean handoff A good escalation is one clear message to the owner, and then you stop.

item.title: 4. After you escalate, it's not yours to carry
item.description: ← Escalation & Handoff After you escalate, it’s not yours to carry This is the most important page in this guide.

item.title: 5. Pressure is not a task
item.description: ← Escalation & Handoff Pressure is not a task The pages before this are about what to do. This one is about the feeling that makes it hard.

item.title: 6. Flow Diagram
item.description: ← Escalation & Handoff Flow Diagram There are two moments to start from: when a request first lands on you, and when a request you’ve already escalated gets pinged again.

item.title: 2. What do I do right now (Flowchart)
item.description: ← Priority Guide ”What do I do right now?” Flowchart Start at the top whenever you finish a piece of work, get blocked, or aren’t sure what’s next.

item.title: 3. Getting Unblocked
item.description: ← Priority Guide Getting Unblocked Precondition — is this work actually yours? This page is about getting unblocked on a review that is already assigned to you.
